artworks.title: Pewit Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds on a cotton plant branch. The scene depicts the birds and the plant with fine attention to detail. One bird is olive-green with a white belly, while the other is cream and grey. The birds are illustrated with sharp detail, showcasing their feathers. This artwork is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Snowy Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of two Snowy Owls perched the branches of a dead tree. The owls have striking white plumage and piercing yellow eyes, and both are perched on branches of a gnarled and weathered tree on the left. The sky behind them is covered in dark blue-gray clouds. The lower owl is facing the left with its head turned towards us, while the owl above it has its torso facing us and its head turned to the right, its chest fluffed up.

artworks.title: Blue Grosbeak
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on a leafy tree. A blue grosbeak and two colorful birds are depicted among lush green leaves on slender branches, with one perched near a nest.

artworks.title: Black and Yellow Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image displays two birds perched on a branch surrounded by green leaves and pink flowers. The birds are predominantly yellow with blue and black markings. There are pink berries and flowers in the background.

artworks.title: Green Black-Capt Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two green birds with yellow bellies are perched amongst large green leaves and pink flowers. The color palette includes various shades of green, pink, and yellow. The composition shows the birds placed amongst the plants and flowers, with one bird slightly elevated on a stem and the other facing leftward.

artworks.title: Brown-Headed Nuthatch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two brown-headed nuthatches on a tree branch. The painting showcases a pair of birds, one in the foreground, clinging upside down to a tree trunk. The birds have brown heads, blue-grey wings, and white bellies. The tree trunk has textures and hints of moss, resembling the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-Headed Eagle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This artwork features a white-headed eagle perched on a branch. The eagle has detailed brown feathers, with its head turned upwards and beak open. The wings and body display brown shades with white edges. The eagle's talons grip the curved branch. The background is plain, emphasizing the eagle. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Rose-breasted Grosbeak
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of several birds perched on branches with a background of foliage. The artwork showcases a group of rose-breasted grosbeaks, among the green needles and small pink and red fruits of a pine-like branch. The birds include both male and female grosbeaks. The composition is balanced, with each bird interacting with different parts of the branch. The detail in the feathers and foliage is remarkable. The stems are slender and curved gracefully. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Cat Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a branch with berries and leaves. The image depicts two birds with gray and black plumage, accented with a hint of red on the lower body, perched on a branch. The branch features clusters of ripening berries in various stages of maturation, from green through red and deep purple. The green leaves surrounding the berries have fine detailing, including visible veins and varying shades of green. The composition captures the birds in different positions.

artworks.title: Great Crested Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds. One bird is flying with its wings fully outstretched, showing detailed feathers in shades of brown and gray, and a vibrant green head. The other bird is perched on a branch, with a mix of green and yellow colors on its body, a bright blue throat, and tail feathers in shades of brown. It sits on a bare, textured branch. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed and life-like bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Yellow-winged Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched among flowers and rocks near a small body of water. The scene captures a Yellow-winged Sparrow standing on a rocky surface surrounded by tall branches with clusters of small pink flowers. Broad leaves add a green contrast to the floral elements. The rocks provide a natural-looking foundation beside a small reflective surface that appears to be a pool or stream. The painting portrays a tranquil, natural habitat, with detailing on the bird's plumage, emphasizing shades of yellow, brown, and gray.

artworks.title: American Robin
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts a family of American Robins on and around a nest built in a tree. Two adult birds and several chicks are visible. The color palette includes various shades of green for the leaves and brown and white for the birds' feathers, with red and rust patches on their chests. One adult robin holds a berry, while another feeds the chicks in the nest. The nest contains two prominent chicks surrounded by leaves in the background.

artworks.title: Three-Toed Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three woodpeckers on a tree branch. The image shows three three-toed woodpeckers perched on a branched tree trunk, each bird displaying a lively posture that emphasizes their unique black and white plumage with a striking yellow crown. Details in their feathers and the bark provide texture and depth to the composition. Surrounding the birds are green and yellow leaves, adding to the natural surroundings.

artworks.title: Black-Poll Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting shows three birds perched on a branch with leaves and berries. The birds are Black-poll Warblers, and the scene depicts them among green and reddish-brown leaves and dark berries. The birds are detailed with black, white, and earth-tone plumage. They appear to be perching in the foliage. The leaves vary in color, suggesting a change of season. The composition is balanced, highlighting the connection between the birds and the natural environment. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's lifelike bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Hemlock Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: There are two yellow birds with black and white markings perched on a vine with large green leaves and clusters of pink flowers. The birds are positioned differently on the vine.

artworks.title: Blackburnian Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A small bird, known as a Blackburnian Warbler, is perched on a branch with pink flowers and green leaves. The color palette includes orange, black, pink, and green against a light background. The bird, branch, flowers, and leaves are arranged diagonally across the canvas.

artworks.title: Meadow Lark
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of meadowlarks amidst lush vegetation. The scene depicts three birds with distinctive yellow breasts, amid detailed greenery with thin, tall stalks adorned with clusters of small, vibrant yellow flowers. The central bird is energetically perched with outspread wings, suggesting a moment of motion. Below, another bird is on the ground, with a visible nest nearby. The foliage creates a dense backdrop, accentuating the natural habitat. The use of precise detailing and vivid colors highlights the lifelike portrayal characteristic of traditional ornithological illustrations.

artworks.title: Yellow-breasted Chat
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of yellow-breasted chats interacting around a nest. The painting depicts three birds with striking yellow breasts and olive-green wings positioned around a nest that is situated in a flowering tree. Two of the birds are in flight with their wings partially open, while the third bird is perched on the edge of the nest which contains a fourth bird sitting within it. The nest is nestled among branches adorned with leaves and flowers, adding a contrast to the birds. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Connecticut Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of birds perched on a branch with flowers. The artwork shows two small birds sitting on a leafy branch. The plant has green leaves and clusters of blue flowers tinged with purple. The birds have detailed plumage; one is green, and the other has a yellow underside and gray head. The painting offers fine attention to details in the feathers of the birds and the textures of the leaves and flowers, against a plain background.

artworks.title: Field Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a field sparrow perched on a rocky surface surrounded by tall, flowering plants and leafy greenery. The bird is brown and white, while the flowers include shades of pink, purple, and green, with berries in blue and red hues. The large leaves and flowering stems frame the bird at the bottom center of the composition on the rocky base, with water visible at the base of the rocks.

artworks.title: Pine Creeping Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a pine tree branch. The illustration depicts two small birds positioned near the top of a diagonally oriented brown branch adorned with slender green pine needles and a pine cone. The bird on the left is drawn in earthy tones, with darker brown on its back and wings complementing its light brown head. The bird on the right showcases a bright yellow underbelly fading into olive-green and black wing feathers. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Goshawk and Stanley Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three hawks in a natural setting. The painting depicts three hawks, each showcasing their distinct features. One hawk is perched on a branch, with detailed brown and white plumage. Another hawk stands with dark grey plumage on its back and wings and a lighter underbelly. Its eyes are red. The third hawk has brown and white plumage and is standing by water. The background includes rocks, grasses, and mountains. The painting is detailed with precision, reminiscent of John James Audubon's style.

artworks.title: American Sparrow Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of American Sparrow Hawks perched on branches. Three American Sparrow Hawks are depicted among lush green leaves and branches. Their vivid plumage is realistically detailed, with vibrant hues of brown, black, red, and white. The birds are positioned in various poses, one perched upright and the others engaging with their surroundings. Their intricate feathers and the detailed foliage evoke a sense of naturalism and lifelike portrayal. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Golden-Crowned Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image displays two birds surrounded by branches and foliage. One bird is brown with a lighter underside perched on a log, while the other bird, primarily white with black stripes, is shown in flight. The color palette consists of earthy tones, with pops of red and orange from berries and mushrooms. The setting features a natural backdrop with the log at the bottom, leaves emerging from it, and the flying bird in the upper right corner among greenery and berries.
